title: 173 Supplementation of vitamin B complex to beef cows during late gestation
content:
Abstract
The main objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of late gestation and early lactation supplementation of a vitamin B complex on the performance of beef cows and their calves. A two-year study (2022 and 2024) was conducted at the Eastern Oregon Agricultural Research Center (EOARC) with a total of 74 mature Angus ´ Hereford cows. Prior to calving, cows were randomly assigned (d0) to one of two treatments: Vitamin (n = 38) or Control (n = 37) in early January, allowing for a minimum of 45 days of supplementation before calving and approximately 15 days post-calving, prior to summer grazing (turnout). During the supplementation phase, cows were fed daily with alfalfa hay to meet maintenance requirements. Cows were individually supplemented 3 times weekly (Monday, Wednesday, and Friday) with dried distiller’s grains fortified or not with a vitamin B complex. The vitamin B complex was provided at 2g/cow daily and, therefore, was provided at 4.7g/cow per feeding event. The vitamin B complex contained pantothenic acid (B5), pyridoxine (B6), folic acid (B9), biotin (B7), and cyanocobalamin (B12). Cows body weight (BW) and body condition score (BCS) were collected monthly, and calf BW was collected at birth and before summer grazing at the turnout. Cows and calves were considered the experiment unit for this study, and all preliminary data were analyzed using the MIXED procedure of SAS (SAS Inst. Inc., Cary, NC, USA). Initial (d0) BW (504 vs. 514 kg, respectively, for Control and Vitamin) and BCS (4.9 vs. 5.0, respectively, for Control and Vitamin) were similar among cows (P ≥ 0.38). No treatment effects (P ≥ 0.61) were observed for BW (550 vs. 556 kg, respectively for Control and Vitamin) or BCS (5.3) among cows post-supplementation. Similarly, no treatment differences (P ≥ 0.58) were observed for cows BW (520 vs. 522 kg respectively for Control and Vitamin) or BCS (5.2) at turnout. Further, no treatment effects (P = 0.63) were observed for calf birth weight (37 kg) or calf BW prior to summer grazing at the turnout (P = 0.30; 74 vs. 77 kg respectively for Control and Vitamin). The supplementation of vitamin B complex in this environment and conditions does not seem to enhance cow-calf performance.
